questions.prompt: Which statement gives the core rule for “Passing messages with queues”?
options: A queue gives a clearer ownership and synchronization boundary than an unprotected global.
The scheduler runs tasks; `vTaskDelay` lets other work use the CPU.
Start with a simple `loop()`; add tasks only for independent work with distinct timing needs.
Each task consumes stack; priority affects scheduler choices.
questions.answer: A queue gives a clearer ownership and synchronization boundary than an unprotected global.
questions.explanation:
A queue gives a clearer ownership and synchronization boundary than an unprotected global.
Why: A queue stores fixed-size items in FIFO order and decouples producer and consumer tasks. `xQueueSend` and `xQueueReceive` can block with a timeout; payloads are copied, so large objects need deliberate pointer-lifetime management. Check the send result instead of silently losing data when a queue is full.
